name: Danger Mouse
notes: The psych-soul producer-arranger who built the modern orchestral soul album. The drum block encodes two subtractions and one repetition, all stated: "dry, tape-compressed live kit with the top end deliberately removed — kick on 1 and 3, damped snare on 2&4 with a short decay, tambourine and handclaps, and **no hi-hat detail**. Long drumless intros are structural, and **a looped 2-bar drum figure often runs unchanged for a whole song**." The removed top end is the lowest hat velocities and a fill density of 0.04; the unchanged loop is why `fills` sit at 16 and 32 bars, the sparsest in the entire section — the kit is not allowed to develop. Harmony is "modal and minor-leaning — `i–VII–VI` and `i–iv` cycles, long pedal-tone passages, and **orchestral reharmonisation on repeats** rather than modulation; the strings change the meaning of a static chord", so both families are the entry's own, chord durations run 4–16 beats for the pedal passages, and the countermelody is a sustain pad carrying the strings and choir. Melody is "hymn-contoured and low-density", which is near-total stepwise motion, an arch-weighted contour, a legato articulation and a very high chord-tone bias. Bass is "played electric bass, simple, root motion in 8ths, entering a section after the guitar; no 808". The entry's headline is that "**the arrangement is the product** — multi-minute instrumental intros and outros, orchestral interludes between tracks, titles split into numbered parts with different tempos", which is the 8-to-32-bar intro and outro. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum probability and velocity and all melody figures; the research sources the producer relationship and the palette and marks the drum/mix detail as inference. ⚠ His kit overlaps the Michael Kiwanuka model by design — he produced those records — and the two are separated by the loop-length and fill behaviour the entry states, not by an invented difference. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 968/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor), and every other lever this gate has was already clean here** — no empty-bar bias, no one-bar phrase length, and no lead allowed to thin below two notes a bar. What was left was the style pool: `generators::counter` can play five answer shapes and this block asked for 2. `answer_lick` is added at weight 2 because the entry already names it — "fuzz/tremolo guitar plus full string section plus gospel-style backing choir is the palette he standardised for this lane; Mellotron, harpsichord and vintage synths as colour" — and the string section is the `sustain_pad` and the doubled guitar the `octave_echo`, but the gospel backing choir answers the lead between its phrases, which is `answer_lick`. ⚠ The weight is INFERRED; the layer it weights is not.
